<fragment>
See also: List of University of Szeged people
The University of Szeged has educated a large number of authors, scientists and athletes. Notable alumni include Nobel laureate scientist Katalin Karikó, opera singer Krisztián Cser,[40] physicists Peter Heszler[41] and László Bela Kish,[42] poets Attila József,[43] Gyula Juhász[44] and Miklós Radnóti,[45] author Mario Szenessy,[46] and Olympic athletes Natasa Janics, Márton Joób and Anita Márton.[47]


Notable professors include Nobel prize-winner Albert Szent-Györgyi, as well as Dezső Csejtei,[48] Sándor Imre,[49] Károly Marót,[50] Ágoston Pável,[51] Antal Szerb,[52] Hildebrand Dezső Várkonyi,[53] István Bibó,[54] Ferenc Finkey,[55] János Martonyi,[56] Gábor Fodor,[57] István Rusznyák,[58] István Apáthy,[59] Zoltán Bay,[60] Lipót Fejér,[61] Alfréd Haar,[61] László Kalmár,[62] Béla Kerékjártó,[63] László Lovász,[64] Tibor Radó,[65] László Rédei,[63] Frigyes Riesz,[61] Béla Szőkefalvi-Nagy[66] and Afwa Thameur.[67]



## See also

[edit]


</fragment>
<fragment>

As a result, the original university was temporarily moved to Szeged in 1921 without any legal or structural changes.[6] At the time, the institution had 62 functioning departments within its four faculties.[6] Between 1922 and 1931, the university saw a great amount of development: teaching hospitals were built along the river Tisza, and other university buildings, including the research institutes on Dóm Square and the Auditorium Maximum at the Faculty of Arts, were built.[6] Among its teachers were Albert Szent-Györgyi, one of the founders of the Faculty of Science, who received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1937 for his discoveries in connection with Vitamin C.[6]


In 1940, the university was divided into two legally separate entities: a smaller part moved back to Cluj, while the larger part remained in Szeged, and was established as a new institution under the name Miklós Horthy University.[5][6]

Twice, the Nobel Prize was awarded for the works performed at the Ioffe Institute. In 1956, academician N. N. Semyonov (together with C. N. Hinshelwood) got the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for a discovery and study of chain reactions: the works were made and published in 1927, when N. N. Semyonov was a staff member of the institute. In 2000, Zh. I. Alferov, director of the Ioffe Institute at that time, became a Nobel Prize laureate in Physics (together with H. Kroemer and J. Kilby) for the development of semiconductor heterostructures for high-speed optoelectronics.


The Ioffe Institute has played a central role in the development of photovoltaic solar power in Russia and internationally, and thus in the development of renewable energy.[2]



## Buildings

[edit]


</fragment>
<fragment>
The Ioffe Institute is considered the cradle of Soviet physics. Such outstanding scientists as L. D. Landau, P. L. Kapitsa started their career here, many physicists — among them Y. B. Zeldovich, I. V. Kurchatov, I. E. Tamm — have worked at the institute for some time.


The research of the institute covers nearly all fields of the contemporary physics, including the solid-state, semiconductors, quantum electronics, astrophysics, plasma, fluid dynamics, cosmology, nuclear synthesis.


More than 100 employees of the institute were recognized by awarding the highest prizes and orders of the Soviet Union and of Russia – in particular the Lenin and State Prizes of the USSR, State Prizes of Russia, Government prizes and special prizes of the Soviet/Russian Academy of Sciences.

Notable faculty in physics have included the speed of light calculator A. A. Michelson, elementary charge calculator Robert A. Millikan, discoverer of the Compton Effect Arthur H. Compton, the creator of the first nuclear reactor Enrico Fermi, "the father of the hydrogen bomb" Edward Teller, "one of the most brilliant and productive experimental physicists of the twentieth century" Luis Walter Alvarez, Murray Gell-Mann who introduced the quark, second female Nobel laureate Maria Goeppert-Mayer, the youngest American winner of the Nobel Prize Tsung-Dao Lee, and astrophysicist Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar.[215]


</fragment>
<fragment>
Further information: List of Nobel laureates affiliated with the University of Chicago

As of October 2020[update], there have been 100 Nobel laureates affiliated with the University of Chicago,[209] 21 of whom were pursuing research or on faculty at the university at the time of the award announcement.[210] Notable alumni and faculty affiliated with the university include 33 Nobel laureates in Economics.[211]


In addition, many Chicago alumni and scholars have won the Fulbright awards[212] and 53 have matriculated as Rhodes Scholars.[27]

In 2019, the University of Chicago claimed 188,000 alumni.[2] While the university's first president, William Rainey Harper stressed the importance of perennial theory over practicality in his institution's curriculum, this has not stopped the alumni of Chicago from being among the wealthiest in the world.[139][140][141]

根据2023年诺贝尔奖获奖者的背景信息，我来为你对比量子点和阿秒物理学这两个重要科学领域的特点：

## **量子点领域**

### **代表人物**
- **Alexey Ekimov**（俄罗斯）- 量子点的发现者和先驱
- **Louis E. Brus**（美国）- 胶体量子点的创造者  
- **Moungi Bawendi**（美国）- 量子点合成技术的发展者

### **科学特点**
- **研究领域**：纳米材料科学、半导体物理、胶体化学
- **核心技术**：量子限制效应、纳米晶体合成、表面化学
- **时间尺度**：主要研究稳态和动力学光学性质
- **应用导向**：高度产业化，技术成熟度高

### **产业化价值**
- **显示技术**：QLED电视、高端显示器已商业化
- **生物医学**：荧光标记、成像、生物传感器
- **太阳能电池**：新型光伏材料
- **LED照明**：高效率、可调谐光源
- **市场规模**：数千亿美元的产业链

---

## **阿秒物理学领域**

### **代表人物**  
- **Anne L'Huillier**（法国/瑞典）- 高次谐波产生的理论奠基者
- **Pierre Agostini**（法国）- 阿秒脉冲产生的实验先驱
- **Ferenc Krausz**（匈牙利/德国）- 阿秒脉冲测量技术发展者

### **科学特点**
- **研究领域**：超快激光物理、原子分子物理、量子电子学
- **核心技术**：高次谐波产生、泵浦-探测技术、飞秒/阿秒激光
- **时间尺度**：10^-18秒（阿秒）的超快过程研究
- **科学导向**：基础科学研究，技术探索性强

### **产业化价值**
- **商业应用**：目前商业化程度较低，主要集中在科研设备
- **潜在应用**：超快光刻、新型电子器件、量子计算、医学成像
- **技术门槛**：极高，需要昂贵的激光设备和精密控制技术
- **市场阶段**：早期技术探索期

---

## **对比分析**

| **方面** | **量子点** | **阿秒物理学** |
|---------|-----------|--------------|
| **成熟度** | 技术成熟，大量商业化 | 前沿研究，技术探索期 |
| **应用广度** | 显示、照明、生物、能源多个领域 | 主要集中在精密测量和基础研究 |
| **产业规模** | 数千亿美元 | 相对较小（科研设备市场） |
| **技术门槛** | 中等，已形成标准化工艺 | 极高，需要尖端设备 |
| **投资回报** | 短期回报高，风险相对低 | 长期基础研究，高风险高回报 |
| **就业机会** | 大量工程和技术岗位 | 主要集中在科研机构 |

---

## **结论**

**量子点技术**已经成功实现了从实验室到产业化的跨越，在多个领域产生了巨大的经济和社会价值，是典型的应用驱动型技术突破。

**阿秒物理学**代表了人类对时间极限认知的重大突破，虽然短期商业价值有限，但为理解物质基本规律提供了前所未有的工具，具有深远的科学意义和长期潜在价值。

这两个领域展现了不同类型的科学突破：一个注重"看得更清"（量子点的光学控制），另一个注重"看得更快"（阿秒的超快观测），共同推动了人类对自然世界的认知边界。

## **量子点领域**

### **代表人物**
- **Alexey Ekimov**（俄罗斯）- 量子点的发现者和先驱
- **Louis E. Brus**（美国）- 胶体量子点的创造者  
- **Moungi Bawendi**（美国）- 量子点合成技术的发展者

### **科学特点**
- **研究领域**：纳米材料科学、半导体物理、胶体化学
- **核心技术**：量子限制效应、纳米晶体合成、表面化学
- **时间尺度**：主要研究稳态和动力学光学性质
- **应用导向**：高度产业化，技术成熟度高

### **产业化价值**
- **显示技术**：QLED电视、高端显示器已商业化
- **生物医学**：荧光标记、成像、生物传感器
- **太阳能电池**：新型光伏材料
- **LED照明**：高效率、可调谐光源
- **市场规模**：数千亿美元的产业链

---

## **阿秒物理学领域**

### **代表人物**  
- **Anne L'Huillier**（法国/瑞典）- 高次谐波产生的理论奠基者
- **Pierre Agostini**（法国）- 阿秒脉冲产生的实验先驱
- **Ferenc Krausz**（匈牙利/德国）- 阿秒脉冲测量技术发展者

### **科学特点**
- **研究领域**：超快激光物理、原子分子物理、量子电子学
- **核心技术**：高次谐波产生、泵浦-探测技术、飞秒/阿秒激光
- **时间尺度**：10^-18秒（阿秒）的超快过程研究
- **科学导向**：基础科学研究，技术探索性强

### **产业化价值**
- **商业应用**：目前商业化程度较低，主要集中在科研设备
- **潜在应用**：超快光刻、新型电子器件、量子计算、医学成像
- **技术门槛**：极高，需要昂贵的激光设备和精密控制技术
- **市场阶段**：早期技术探索期

---

| **投资回报** | 短期回报高，风险相对低 | 长期基础研究，高风险高回报 |
| **就业机会** | 大量工程和技术岗位 | 主要集中在科研机构 |

---

**量子点技术**已经成功实现了从实验室到产业化的跨越，在多个领域产生了巨大的经济和社会价值，是典型的应用驱动型技术突破。

## **Top Universities for Nobel Alumni**

### **1. Harvard University** 🏆

- Over 160 Nobel laureates affiliated (including alumni, faculty, and researchers)

- Notable alumni include numerous winners across all Nobel categories

### **3. Humboldt University of Berlin (Germany)**
- **Rich scientific heritage** with revolutionary impact
